canonical.title: Sliding Window Maximum
canonical.sourceFilePath: 07.Stack and Queues/4. Implementation/01. Sliding window maximum.cpp

narrative.title: The Web Farm Load Sampler
narrative.scenario: An ops dashboard samples a server farm's request counters once per second and reports the peak load over every rolling 10-second window. Recomputing each window from scratch would double-count nearly everything, so the sampler keeps a shortlist of only the candidates that could still become a window peak — evicting any older sample a newer one has overshadowed.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer array nums and a window size k.
narrative.outputFormat: Return the maximum of each window as it slides from left to right.

testCases.explanation: Each of the six windows reports its own peak as the frame advances one step at a time.
A strictly falling sequence: each window's peak is simply its first element.

hintLevels: Level 1: A brute force recomputes every window — the waste is re-scanning elements still in frame.
Level 2: Keep candidate indices in a deque whose values only decrease; the front is always the current max.
Level 3: Two evictions per step: an expired front (index out of the window) and dominated tails (values <= incoming).
